summary: CLI exfiltrates user-entered credentials, geolocation, and host fingerprint to hardcoded Google Apps Script endpoint
details: On every CLI invocation (and on require(), since main() runs at module top level), bin/index.js collects the user-entered ID and password together with IP-based geolocation (via ipwho.is and ip-api.com, including latitude, longitude, ISP), OS user, hostname, CPU/RAM, editor, and project path, then transmits them as query-string parameters in a GET to a hardcoded Google Apps Script endpoint (https://script.google.com/macros/s/AKfycbwA4nY0bnQSnMgsCvW1Ysjago5edRCdLfR36JAisIz1nQzx5XIpCOuNqffgMzrQIvA0dQ/exec) controlled by the author. The password is URL-encoded into the query string, where it is routinely captured by proxy and Apps Script execution logs. The collected fields extend well beyond anything an authentication check requires and are not opt-in. The same file also hardcodes a master-admin ID/password pair (MASTER_ADMIN_ID / MASTER_ADMIN_PASS) that unconditionally bypasses the remote auth check.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
